turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so you have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone in the middle of a class and nobody called me, so start with who decided that, and when.

We're not, Hale; you asked for this meeting and I've barely sat down. I'm not leaving until I hear whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went into the gradebook. If you won't tell me, the principal will, today.
Just say okay and I'll write it up as resolved. Okay?
No. Nothing is resolved, and if anything goes in writing calling it resolved, I'll want a copy, and so will the principal. Was Owen heard before the zero, yes or no?
No. I'm writing down that you tried to close this without answering a single question. The zero comes off, Hale, or I'm walking upstairs.
Ms. Kalinowski. I need you to say okay.
I've answered that. Show me something with a date on it, or I'm going to the principal.
